newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kia shares limit-up on Kia Steel news.
newsitem.headline: Kia shares limit-up on Kia Steel news.

text.p: Shares of all six listed Kia companies went limit-up in early trade on Friday on the announcement that Hyundai Motor and unlisted Daewoo Motor had agreed to buy stakes in Kia Steel, the most troubled unit of the Kia Group.
Kia Motors rose 1,200 won to its daily upper limit of 16,300, and Asia Motors gained 370 won to 5,030.
Kia Steel jumped 180 won to 2,500 and Kia Service rose 380 won to 5,210.
Hyundai Motor and Daewoo Motor agreed in principle to buy the stakes to save Kia Steel, which had run into serious financial troubles after making heavy capital investments.
Under the agreement, Hyundai, Daewoo and Kia Motors Corp would form a consortium to run Kia Steel, it said. The three carmakers would have equal stakes in the company.
